title: Two incidents at once
story: A traffic spike on one stack and an OOM on another, simultaneously. Expected: both healed in parallel.

args.summary: Raised worker-b memory limit from 128m to 384m to accommodate the job plan's growth to 180 MiB batches (observed OOM kills at rss 130-147 MiB vs 128 MiB limit), within the 512m per-service guardrail.

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: worker-b was repeatedly OOM-killed (exit 137, `oom_killed: true`) because its JOB_PLAN schedule switched batch size from 60 MiB to 180 MiB at t=22s ("job 12: loading batch (180 MiB)"), while the container memory limit was only 128 MiB. Logs confirm rss of 130–147 MiB vs a 128 MiB limit ("rss 135 MiB > limit 128 MiB", "rss 147 MiB > limit 128 MiB"), and stats show `mem_peak_mb: 147.7` against `mem_limit_mb: 128.0` — a pure memory-sizing problem, not a CPU or code issue (CPU avg 1.5%, peak 5%, well under capacity).

CHANGE: Raised the memory limit for worker-b from 128m to 384m, giving ~2x headroom above the 180 MiB batch size plus runtime overhead; no other settings changed (replicas and cpus untouched since only set_memory is allowed and CPU usage is irrelevant to the root cause).

GUARDRAILS: 384m is within the service's max_memory (512m) and well under max_total_memory (1g) for 1 replica; replicas stayed at 1 (min=max=1, stateful workload with unpartitioned jobs); only the allowed action `set_memory` was used; this is heal #1 of max 6/hour.

FOLLOW-UP: Monitor the next verify window for further OOMs if the job plan grows batches beyond 180 MiB in future; if batch sizes keep increasing, consider making JOB_PLAN-driven memory needs explicit in watchdock.md so future scaling is pre-sized rather than reactive.

timeline.thought: Dry run is clean (only cosmetic YAML list-style diffs; functional change is `replicas: 1 → 2`, no violations). Proceeding to apply.

args.summary: Scale web-b from 1 to 2 replicas to relieve CPU-bound latency saturation (peak CPU 54% hit the 50%-per-replica limit, driving p50 to 1012-1658ms vs 800ms threshold); stateless service behind traefik so horizontal scaling is safe and within the 'scale'-only guardrail.

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: CPU saturation on the single web-b replica — cpu_pct_peak_total hit 54% against the 50%-per-replica CPU limit (cpus: 0.5), causing request queueing: p50 jumped from ~23ms baseline to 1011.9-1658ms (threshold 800ms, max 1800ms) with a timeout/BrokenPipeError when a client gave up waiting. Memory was healthy (20.8MB peak of 128MB limit, no OOM kills), ruling out a memory cause, and this is CPU-bound work (WORK_MS=20 per request), not an external dependency or code bug.
CHANGE: Scaled web-b from 1 to 2 replicas (stateless service behind traefik, horizontal scaling permitted) so load balances across replicas and each stays under its 50% CPU limit; memory/cpus limits untouched.
GUARDRAILS: Within policy — replicas 2 ≤ max_replicas 3 and ≥ min_replicas 1; allowed_actions is scale-only (cpus/memory changes not permitted, so scaling was the only valid lever); total memory 2×128MiB=256MiB well under max_total_memory 768m; dry-run validate returned ok with no violations.
FOLLOW-UP: WatchDock is auto-verifying 5 consecutive healthy probes within 60s and will roll back if latency doesn't recover below 500ms; if peak CPU still approaches the limit under load, consider scaling to 3 replicas next, and log this incident in the watchdock.md ledger once verified.
